VI.}}</noinclude>vve shal be also of his resurrection. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=6}}† Knovving this, that our {{sup|‖}} old man is crucified vvith him, that the body of sinne may be {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Castalion noteth that Beza falsely translateth ''enervetur,'' for, ''destruatur:'' weakened, for, destroyed.}}∷ destroied, to the end that vve may serue sinne no longer. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=7}}† For he that is dead, is iustified from sinne. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=8}}† And if vve be dead vvith Christ, vve beleeue that vve shal liue also together vvith Christ. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=9}}† knovving that Christ rising againe from the dead, novv dieth no more, death shal no more haue dominion ouer him. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=10}}† For that he died, {{sup|‖}} to sinne he died once: but that he liueth, he liueth to God. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=11}}† So thinke you also, that you are dead to sinne, but aliue to God in Christ {{sc|Iesvs}} our Lord.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=12}}† Let not {{sup|‖}} sinne therfore reigne in your mortal body, that you obey the concupiscences thereof. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=13}}† But neither doe ye exhibite your members instruments of iniquitie vnto sinne: but exhibite your selues to God as of dead men, aliue: and your members instruments of iustice to God. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=14}}† For sinne shal not haue dominion ouer you. for you are not vnder the Lavv, but vnder grace. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=15}}† VVhat then? shal vve sinne, because vve are not vnder the Lavv, but vnder grace? God forbid. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=16}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 8, 34. 2. Pet. 2, 19.''}}* Knovv you not that to vvhom you exhibite your selues seruants to obey, you are the seruants of him vvhom you obey, vvhether it be of sinne, to death, or of obedience, to iustice. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=17}}† But thankes be to God, that you vvere the seruants of sinne, but {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here againe is signified, that our discharge frō the bōdage of sinne, is by the Christian faith, & by obedience to the whole doctrine of Christs religion: in that the Apostle attributeth this their deliuerance frō sinne, to their humble receiuing of the Catholike faith.}}∷ haue obeied from the hart, vnto that {{sup|‖}} forme of doctrine, into the vvhich you haue been deliuered. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=18}}† And being made free from sinne, you vvere made seruants to iustice. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=19}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō the 7 Sunday after Pentecost.}}I speake an humane thing, because of the infirmitie of your flesh. for as you haue exhibited your members to serue vncleannesse and iniquitie, vnto iniquitie: so now exhibite your members to serue iustice, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He signifieth that as when they vvere subiect to sinne by cōtinual & oftē working wickednes, they increased their iniquitie: that so also novv being iustified, they may & should by external vvorkes of Iustice, increase their iustice and sanctification.}}∷ vnto sanctification. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=20}}† For when you vvere seruants of sinne, you were free to iustice. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=21}}† What fruite therfore had you then in those things, for vvhich novv you are ashamed? for the end of them is death. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=22}}† But novv being made free from sinne, and become seruants to God, you haue your fruite vnto sanctification, but the end, life euerlasting. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=23}}† For the stipends of sinne, death. but {{sup|‖}} the grace of God, life euerlasting in Christ {{sc|Iesvs}} our Lord.⊣
